::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
IISc Bengaluru spin-off (CEO Hareesh Chandrasekar, co-founder Srinivasan Raghavan) built on over 15 years of GaN research at IISc. Not strictly fabless; it owns the whole GaN chain from epitaxial wafers to devices, which are made at IISc's MeitY-funded GaN Ecosystem Enabling Centre and Incubator (GEECI), housed in CeNSE (see the facility page). Raised a $3.5 million seed round (3one4 Capital, Zephyr Peacock) in October 2024 and a $2.6 million extension (Shastra VC) in March 2026. It runs customer pilots, has begun pilot wafer exports, holds an iDEX contract for GaN wireless transmitters, and targets 1 lakh chips a year; it has also said it wants a GaN factory under Semicon 2.0.
:::

## What does this firm design?

GaN-on-silicon/SiC epitaxial wafers, RF transistors and power devices for defence radar and communications, telecom base stations and power electronics.

**Why these scores**

- **Domain difficulty 4/5:** GaN RF transistors and power devices for radar and base stations; compound-semiconductor RF work.
- **IP ownership 5/5:** Owns the full GaN chain, from epitaxial wafers to device design, built on 15 years of IISc research.
- **Design completeness 4/5:** Devices made at IISc's GEECI line; customer pilots and pilot wafer exports show working parts.
- **Market readiness 3/5:** Customer pilots, pilot wafer exports and an iDEX contract; 1 lakh chips a year is still a target.
